topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes, cancer progression model, and the framework of the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway mutations
topics.groupedBecause: They detail how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin pathways enable growth signal independence and resistance to growth-inhibitory cues.

topics.label: Blocks to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how differentiation arrest contributes to tumorigenesis using hematological malignancies and colorectal intestinal epithelium as examples.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the molecular balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins and how p53 pathway disruptions allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, telomere regulation, and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: They describe telomere maintenance, telomerase reactivation, and how cancer cells bypass senescence and p53-mediated stress responses to achieve replicative immortality.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: They introduce complex non-cell-autonomous hallmarks and describe how cancer cells rewire their metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific profiles, and oncometabolite-generating mutations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the angiogenic switch and the molecular balance regulating blood vessel recruitment required for tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They cover the multistep metastatic cascade, circulation dynamics, liquid biopsy detection, metastatic inefficiency, and the genomic features of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of how cancer hallmarks integrate and offers closing remarks.
